 Lone Star Suffer 4-2 Defeat to Cabo Verde 
 —As AFCON Hopes Fade 
 By Peter Bayor Bishop
 Nov 14, 2026 
 Nov 14, 2026

 Liberia’s campaign in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers suffered another major setback on Friday after the Lone Star succumbed to a 4-2 defeat against Cabo Verde in a Group K encounter at the Estadio Nacional de Cabo Verde in Praia.
 Despite showing occasional attacking promise, Liberia struggled defensively, particularly in dealing with aerial deliveries and set pieces, while costly goalkeeping errors further compounded the team's problems.
 The defeat leaves Liberia rooted at the bottom of Group K in fourth place, while Cabo Verde strengthened its position in third, further complicating the Lone Star's qualification prospects.
 The hosts wasted little time exposing Liberia's defensive weaknesses, taking the lead just five minutes into the encounter.
 A well-delivered pass from João Paulo sliced through the Liberian defense, allowing Ayoni Santos to capitalize on hesitation involving center-back Sampson Dweh before firing Cabo Verde into a 1-0 lead.
 Cabo Verde maintained control of possession for much of the opening half, forcing Liberia to spend extended periods defending deep inside its own territory.
 However, against the run of play, the Lone Star found an equalizer in the 36th minute when Franklin Nyenetue capitalized on a loose cross to bring Liberia level at 1-1, briefly silencing the home supporters in Praia.
 Liberia's celebrations were short-lived, as Cabo Verde restored its advantage less than two minutes later.
 In the 38th minute, Rocha Tavares rose unchallenged from a corner kick and directed a powerful header beyond goalkeeper Ashley Williams to make it 2-1.
 The defensive problems continued to haunt Liberia five minutes later. In the 43rd minute, Dailon Livramento took advantage of another breakdown in the Lone Star's aerial organization, heading home from close range as Liberian defenders failed to challenge effectively.
 The goal extended Cabo Verde's lead to 3-1 heading into halftime, leaving Liberia with a difficult task in the second period.
 After the restart, the Lone Star pushed forward in search of a comeback, attempting to reduce the deficit and regain a foothold in the contest.
 However, their attacking efforts left spaces at the back, which Cabo Verde eventually exploited during stoppage time.
 D. Sanches Fernandes struck in the 90+2nd minute to increase the hosts' advantage to 4-1, seemingly putting the result beyond doubt.
 Liberia managed to pull one goal back three minutes later when forward Ayouba Kosiah converted a penalty in the 90+5th minute, reducing the deficit to 4-2.
 The late consolation goal, however, could not prevent another disappointing result for the Lone Star.
 Erradi Defends Team Despite Defeat
 Speaking after the match, Liberia's head coach, Mohamed Erradi, defended his players' performance, arguing that the team was still undergoing a rebuilding process and had not enjoyed sufficient preparation time to compete consistently against more established opponents.
 While acknowledging the defeat, Erradi expressed satisfaction with the commitment shown by his players, pointing to the experience and collective understanding of the Cabo Verde team as important factors in the outcome.
 "To be honest with you, I am proud of my players and what they did on the field," Erradi stated. "We played against a high-level team with strong individuality, and we couldn't control some key moments in the first and second halves. We lost the game, yes, but we are building our team."
 The Liberian coach noted that Cabo Verde's core group of players had been together for approximately five to six years, giving them an advantage in terms of tactical understanding, coordination, and collective experience.
 He also referenced similar long-term football development projects in Mali and Rwanda, emphasizing that sustained preparation and continuity are essential to building competitive national teams.
 Erradi explained that he had only spent about two months assembling and assessing the current Liberian squad, with just one international friendly against Sierra Leone before the team's competitive assignments.
 "Two months is not enough to build a high-level team to compete against this kind of opponent," Erradi argued.
 "We didn't have enough time or friendly games to discover and know our players, yet their defensive and offensive behavior is changing. We are on the right path, but we need time, a new work approach, and more tools to build a balanced, competitive team."
 Coach Explains Goalkeeping Decisions
 Erradi also addressed the goalkeeping problems that contributed to Liberia's defeat, particularly the errors that led to Ashley Williams being substituted before halftime.
 The coach explained that injuries to the team's first-choice goalkeepers during the matches against Rwanda and Mali had forced his technical staff to make difficult decisions regarding the position.
 According to Erradi, Williams had initially been introduced during the warm-up of the match against Mali following an injury and subsequently delivered a strong performance.
 He said the technical staff therefore considered that performance when selecting Williams to start against Cabo Verde, despite having recently identified another goalkeeper in Nigeria.
 "We brought Ashley in during the warm-up against Mali after an injury, and he performed very well," Erradi noted.
 "Even though we recently discovered a new goalkeeper in Nigeria, as professionals, we had to respect Ashley's performance against Mali and give him the start. Today simply wasn't his day—he made mistakes, and we had to substitute him in the first half to protect him. That is normal in football."
 The coach's explanation comes amid growing concerns about the Lone Star's defensive organization and the team's ability to maintain concentration during crucial moments of international competition.
 Pressure Mounts as Qualification Hopes Diminish
 While Erradi remains confident that Liberia is making progress under his rebuilding approach, the latest defeat is likely to intensify pressure on the technical team as supporters continue to question the national team's performances.
 The four goals conceded against Cabo Verde, particularly the repeated defensive lapses from set pieces and crosses, have again exposed areas requiring urgent attention.
 For Liberia, the challenge now extends beyond individual match results to addressing deeper concerns surrounding squad preparation, defensive coordination, goalkeeping stability, and the overall development of a competitive national team.
 With the Lone Star still occupying the bottom position in Group K, the margin for further setbacks has narrowed considerably.
 Although Erradi has called for patience, additional preparation time, and improved technical support, Liberian supporters will be looking for tangible improvements on the pitch as the national team attempts to restore confidence and keep its AFCON qualification ambitions alive.
